q: A real number x ∈ [0,1] is computable if:
opts: There is a Turing machine that, given n, outputs a rational q with |x-q| < 2^{-n}
x can be written as a finite decimal
x is algebraic (satisfies a polynomial equation with integer coefficients)
exp: Computable reals: a Turing machine approximates x to arbitrary precision. Most reals are not computable (countably many computable reals, uncountably many reals). Computable ≠ algebraic: π and e are computable but transcendental; Chaitin's Ω is neither algebraic nor computable.
